summary: The study reports on the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of indium oxide (In2O3) using a novel liquid precursor, [3-(dimethylamino)propyl]dimethyl indium (DADI), and water vapor as the oxidant. The deposited In2O3 films exhibit low resistivity (9.2 × 10^-5 Ω cm) and high optical transparency (>80% between 420 and 700 nm). The process achieves a growth rate of 0.6 Å/cycle at 275 °C, with the films showing high carrier concentration and low resistivity due to oxygen vacancies or In interstitials. The study highlights the advantages of using a liquid precursor for ALD, enabling the synthesis of high-conductivity transparent films at moderate temperatures.
evidence: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) of In2O3 films was investigated using a novel liquid precursor, [3-(dimethylamino)propyl]dimethyl indium (DADI). Typical ALD growth was observed at a substrate temperature of 275 °C, with relatively high growth rates of 0.6 Å/cycle. The In2O3 layer exhibits low resistivity (9.2 × 10^-5 Ω cm) with relatively high optical transparency ( >80% between 420 and 700 nm). The carrier concentration is approximately one or two orders of magnitude higher than those reported in the literature. The origin of such electrical properties is investigated with respect to the microstructure and chemical properties of the In2O3 film.
